measured.note: a linear trend of the in-plane shift with z is what a rigid rotation between the two frames looks like; it does not say which frame (CT placement, photograph frame, or the body between acquisitions) carries it

extrapolated.note: a linear trend of the in-plane shift with z is what a rigid rotation between the two frames looks like; it does not say which frame (CT placement, photograph frame, or the body between acquisitions) carries it

method.photo_body: R > B + 25 and max(R,G,B) > 60, rows below 1000, closing, fill holes, components >= 200 blocks of 4 x 4 px
method.ct_body: HU > -400 sampled on the photograph grid through the transform and the CT placement, fill holes, components >= 200
method.photo_bone: inside body, R > 165, G > 150, B > 120, R - B < 70 (a colour threshold; informative only)
method.shift: phase correlation of the signed distance transforms (clipped at 20 blocks), 10 x upsampled
method.z_scan: body Dice at z + dz, dz -15..15 mm step 1.5, parabolic peak; at_edge counts scans whose best lies on the scan limit (inconclusive)

limits: the floor of this comparison is the CT placement (rigid pelvis fit, p95 5.4 mm, angular error grows with distance from the pelvis) plus the fresh-CT versus frozen-block outline difference; nothing here separates them
above the pelvis the mapping is the pelvis block extrapolated; the excess over the measured-mapping baseline is the alignment uncertainty of the photographs there, not a correction
photograph bone is a colour threshold; the CT arms lie partly outside the CT field of view (423 slices on the edge)
